[[Broughton, Flintshire|Broughton]] | capacity = 1,600 (500 seated){{cite web |url=http://airbusfc.com/index.php/club/stadium |title=Stadium |access-date=1 March 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20140301235701/http://airbusfc.com/index.php/club/stadium |archive-date=1 March 2014 }} | owner = Broughton Wings Sports and Social Club | chairman = Michael Mayfield | manager = Mark Allen | league = {{Welsh football updater|AirbusB}} | season = {{Welsh football updater|AirbusB2}} | position = {{Welsh football updater|AirbusB3}} | website = https://www.airbusukfc.com/ | pattern_la1 = _blueborder | pattern_b1 = _whitecollar | pattern_ra1 = _blueborder| | pattern_b2 = | leftarm1 = FFFFFF | body1 = 0000FF | rightarm1 = FFFFFF | shorts1 = 0000ff | socks1 = 0000ff | leftarm2 = 8D0730 | body2 = 8D0730 | rightarm2 = 8D0730 | shorts2 = 8D0730 | socks2 = 8D0730 }} '''Airbus UK Broughton Football Club''' is a semi-professional [[association football|football]] club based in [[Broughton, Flintshire]], [[Wales]]. They had their origins as the [[works team]] of the [[Airbus UK]] factory in Broughton where the wings of [[Airbus]] aircraft are produced, and are consequently nicknamed ''The Wingmakers'' or ''The Planemakers''. They play in the {{Welsh football updater|AirbusB}}. The club was promoted to the [[Cymru Premier]] for the first time in 2004, and play at [[The Airfield|The Hollingsworth Group Stadium]] (previously known as [[The Airfield]]), [[Broughton, Flintshire|Broughton]] (capacity 1,600, of which 500 are seated); however as their pitch could not be brought up to Cymru Premier standards in time following their promotion, for their first two games they shared [[Conwy United F.C.|Conwy United]]'s ground. The Airfield features three unusual retracting floodlights as it is adjacent to an operational runway. In 2014, the grass surface was replaced with a 3G synthetic pitch. At the end of the 2016–17 season the club were relegated to the [[Cymru Alliance]] having finished bottom of the league. In the 2022–23 season, the club finished with -4 points after being deducted 6 points and losing all but two matches. As a result, they were relegated back to the [[Cymru North]] after having been promoted in the 2021–22 season."}}
